title: Promising results

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Nice run, and it's good that you say the last day had two big losses. A record like this, mostly small wins with a few large losses, is exactly how these contracts behave, so I'd look at the largest single loss as a share of the account, since scaling up makes that number bigger. The fee and spread on each fill also matter more as size grows, and thin books may not fill your size at the screen price. If you also like trading around news and events, Cymetica's Event Cards are another way to do it with stocks and crypto.

replies.author: Weak_Wallaby734
replies.body:
Got news filters in there. I’ve tested fills. With really high contract amounts, I get filled fully.

Zero fees, and I am the spread 👀

replies.author: Illustrious_Web_2774
replies.body: How can you manage zero fees. I rely on LOs as well but unless you can perfectly predict the price movement, you'd end up being taker every now and then?

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: That makes sense, as a maker you don't pay the taker fee and you earn the spread. The risk on that side is that you tend to get filled right when the price is about to move against you, so the losses can come in bursts. I'd track the average result right after each fill, not just the daily total, since that shows how much of the spread the moves take back.

I initially started with $50 and it has grown from there.  
By the end of this week I plan on starting withdraws, 2-3x a week.

replies.author: Weak_Wallaby734
replies.body:
Roughly 4-5 hours a day for about 2 months. The last 2 weeks have been just checking on everything about 1h a day.

I got really into it, and it’s costed me about 1-2k in losses while making everything finally work. And I can say I’m finally in the green.

Demo trading isn’t viable. Live data live trades is best with a disposable amount of income. You learn and gain real world data rather then skewed results from back tests. Using demo to trade live results also isn’t promising. You’d miss out on finding out what really fills in real money situations.
